title: Why Blanton was different from other bass players
summary: Greer says Blanton played horn solos on bass and inspired later bassists.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I heard some good bass players, Oscar Peterson --
Pettiford. And the boy who played -- who plays with Merv Griffin now.
Ray Brown. I played with all them guys.
Old "Big'un", he's something else. But this guy, he started a brand new innovation for bass players when they heard him, you know. He was something, man.
What was it that separated him from the rest of the bass players?

Well, I don't know. Well, you know, he could hear a horn or something play a different solo on his instrument, and he could turn around and play it on his bass. That's what separated him. A lot of records he'd play, you can detect a different trumpet player's solo or different guy's solo, he could do it right on the bass, you know. That's on the record. But he was the first one I heard play -- I don't think I'm wrong but he was the inspiration for Oscar, all them boys.
I know it. They all know it.
Yeah, everybody's gone on record as saying --
Yeah, they know that. He's something else.
